claim: When the memory-unavailable AgentRunError is raised, the failed turn is not recorded in the conversation store as a successful assistant answer. Later turns in the same conversation do not inherit an answer that was produced without saved memory.
verify_against: Where query_database_impl_with_widgets (or its caller in server.py) writes turns into the conversation store, relative to the open_error raise
verify_hint: Look for conversation_store calls in query_database.py and server.py query_database handler; before or after the AgentRunError raise
evidence: In src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py the memory-unavailable AgentRunError is raised at ~lines 719-735, after agent.send_message has fully run (lines ~627-640) and the turn lock block has exited. The agent persists its messages into conversation_store during send_message. The only post-run store manipulation is _trim_unanswered_tool_use (removes only an unanswered tool_use) and _rollback_conversation, which is only called in the asyncio.CancelledError branch. Neither runs on the open_error path, so the turn's assistant answer stays in the store and later turns on the same conversation inherit it. server.py:378 only catches AgentRunError for formatting and does not touch the store.

This must hold on the show_details-off path too, where server.py re-raises AgentRunError and FastMCP's Tool.run builds the error text.

When the server's vector memory store could not be opened, the call

verify_against: FastMCP tool-error wrapping when a tool raises a non-ToolError exception
verify_hint: Check mcp.server.fastmcp.tools.base.Tool.run and call_tool against the AgentRunError re-raise branch in server.py
evidence: query_database.py:723-735 raises AgentRunError(_MEMORY_UNAVAILABLE_MESSAGE) (text begins 'Memory store unavailable: ', line 99) when agent_memory.open_error is set; AgentRunError.__init__ calls super().__init__(message) (lines 69-77) so str(exc) is that message; the raise is outside the try/except at 687 that remaps to internal error. show_details-off: agent_trace None -> server.py:378-384 re-raises; mcp Tool.run (base.py:116-117) wraps as ToolError('Error executing tool query_database: Memory store unavailable: ...'), giving isError. show_details-on: server.py:385 returns _trace_error_result whose text is f'Error executing tool query_database: {message}' (server.py:185-190). Both paths match the docstring at server.py:357-360.

claim: open_error is typed `BaseException | None`, but _get_client records only `Exception` subclasses. If a BaseException that is not an Exception escapes PersistentClient (for example a CancelledError when the open runs in an executor or task), it is not recorded and does not clear a stale earlier record.
verify_against: The except Exception block in ChromaAgentMemory._get_client and its executor callers
verify_hint: Read _get_client's except clause and callers via self._executor
evidence: agent_memory.py:124 types _open_error as BaseException | None and :155 open_error returns BaseException | None. _get_client (:136-152) wraps PersistentClient in `except Exception as exc: self._open_error = exc; raise`, so a non-Exception BaseException is not recorded and the `self._open_error = None` at :150 is skipped, leaving any stale earlier record. The literal mechanics hold. The CancelledError example is unrealistic: _get_client runs inside a ThreadPoolExecutor thread (run_in_executor), and asyncio cancellation is delivered to the awaiting task, not raised inside the worker thread. Only KeyboardInterrupt or SystemExit-type exceptions could escape there, and rarely. The gap is real but low-impact, and the example is inaccurate.

claim: The test docstring claims a workflow-handled message makes no model call and no store open. The stub-based test never checks that no open was attempted, so the claim needs a falsification attempt against the real workflow handler.
source_excerpt: A workflow-handled message (no model, no open) reports an earlier recorded failure.
verify_against: The real default workflow handler's handling of `help` and whether it touches agent_memory before the model is called
verify_hint: Trace the workflow handler under src/sqllens/agent/core/ for any agent_memory access (search/get_recent_memories -> _get_client) before the model is called; settle by reading source only
evidence: The real DefaultWorkflowHandler.try_handle (src/sqllens/agent/core/workflow/default.py:56-95) handles 'help' by building a static string. It checks only user.group_memberships and returns WorkflowResult(should_skip_llm=True) with a RichTextComponent. It never touches agent_memory, search, get_recent_memories or ChromaAgentMemory._get_client. In Agent.send_message (src/sqllens/agent/core/agent/agent.py), the steps before the workflow check are the status bar yield, the in-process conversation_store.get_conversation, observability spans and before_message lifecycle hooks (about lines 357-452). None of these access agent_memory. The factory (src/sqllens/agent/factory.py) registers no lifecycle hooks (grep found none). The workflow check at about lines 454-472 skips the LLM when should_skip_llm is true. So a help turn makes no model call and does not open the store. The open_error check in query_database.py:723-731 reads the shared memory's recorded open_error attribute without opening the store, which matches the test's claim that the turn reports an earlier recorded failure. One caveat: the test itself uses a stub agent, but the docstring's claim about the real code path holds.
